# Independent audit: arbitrary planar convex bodies and union-tail stability

Audited `candidate 94bf8f29da63e55b`
in full. Result: **PASS**, with no mathematical correction required.

The exact proved scope is every full-dimensional compact convex planar
body Q that is within 10^(-6) of a triangle in some affine Hausdorff
frame. One constructed enclosing triangle S satisfies

    1-|Q|/|S| <=180[D(Q)-4/9],
    dist_cap(mu_Q,mu_S)<=1-|Q|/|S|.

This is a finite ordinary-body statement, including smooth boundaries;
it is not a conclusion obtained by passing an unquantified remainder
through polygon approximations.

## 1. Support-point normalization

The eroded inner triangle inclusion follows correctly from
T_inner+[-delta,delta]^2 subset T and the Hausdorff support estimate.
The three selected line intersections exist and have the stated
coordinate bounds. Every chosen support at those points has the
required orientation: the inner triangle supplies interior points to
the right, above, or below the corresponding contact. The slope bounds
therefore apply to arbitrary supporting lines, not only polygon sides.

I independently checked the two-by-two denominator and numerator
bounds, boundedness of the resulting three-halfplane intersection,
the vertex bounds 6delta and30delta, the inverse-matrix estimate,
the contact-point error44delta, and the determinant/area estimate
tau<=81delta. No optimizing triangle or affine map is invoked.

## 2. Exact missing-set representation and the infinite-union issue

The strict exterior support caps give exactly S\Q. Any nonempty one
excludes one S vertex strictly. If another vertex were excluded or
on its boundary, the retained interior point of their S edge would
also be strictly excluded. Thus every cap is a genuine one-vertex
triangle with both incident intercepts positive and at most
1/2+44delta. Its normalized area is their product and is at most tau,
so a short intercept is uniformly below1/100.

Each orientation union is an arbitrary union of relatively open
halfspace traces in S, hence relatively open and Borel. No countable
indexing or measurable selection of support directions is needed.
Including a two-short cut in both orientation classes is harmless;
each class remains a subset of its vertex union.

The proof correctly avoids inferring disjointness from an uncountable
collection of pairwise null intersections. Fix the single retained
contact of the edge joining vertices i,j, with barycentrics t,1-t.
For any actual point in both strict vertex unions, their respective
witness cuts give

    lambda_j<t(1-lambda_k/B),
    lambda_i<(1-t)(1-lambda_k/B), B<1.

Their sum contradicts lambda_i+lambda_j=1-lambda_k. Therefore the
ENTIRE strict vertex unions are disjoint, not just almost disjoint.
This remains valid if Q is smooth and the selected support touches
at only one point. Positive-length retained edges are unnecessary.

## 3. One map for each whole orientation union

For every constituent u/a+v/b<1 with b<=B, the map

    (u,v) -> (u/r,(v-s)/r),
    s=309/1000, r=1-s/B=64/167,

sends its v>=s portion into the SAME strict triangle. In particular
b>s follows from strict membership, and both image coordinates are
nonnegative. The calculation remains strict before the final bound
1-s/b<=1-s/B. The map is injective, all sets and images are Borel,
and its determinant is r^(-2). Thus the exact tail coefficient r^2
holds for the whole union, regardless of overlaps or cardinality.
The barycentric-to-Euclidean area factor cancels. The coefficient is
sharp for one triangle with long intercept exactly B.

## 4. All-direction loss accounting and one actual point

The low-volume S-cap lemma and both rational product gaps are the
same independently proved all-normal lemma used for quadrilaterals.
The vertex2 trace threshold exceeds309/1000. A cap at a short
neighbor misses the entire orientation union, and the other neighbor
loses at most3/20 of that union's mass.

The definitions

    L_i=tau_i+(3/20)sum_(j!=i)|O_(j,i)|/|S|

are simultaneous upper bounds for the same physical cap directions.
Since each orientation is contained in its vertex union,
0<=L_i<=tau and sum L_i<=13tau/10. Counting own union mass only
once is essential and is done correctly. No number-of-cuts factor
survives this step.

The candidate coordinates sum to one, stay inside the coefficient
window, and lie in int Q: a whole neighborhood has every barycentric
coordinate greater than1/100, whereas every missing cap has a short
coordinate below that value. The three product-cap lower bounds and
the high-cap gap consequently cover ALL containing halfspaces at
this actual point. The exact normalized remainder is

    tau(1-404tau)/[180(1-tau)]>=0.

The nested normalized TV identity is correct. The source does not
import the pentagon-specific lower cap-distance bound tau/2; only
the valid upper bound is used for arbitrary Q.

## 5. Independent exact checks

The separate standard-library verifier
`supporting computation verify_all_planar_union_homothety_functional_audit.py` passes
**7911 exact rational checks**. It computes exact affine-envelope
union areas for301 overlapping families of up to23 vertex triangles,
checks the same-triangle tail map and its sharp coefficient, and
constructs24 actual many-cut convex polygons. For those bodies it
checks exact vertex-union area, orientation accounting, the candidate,
and80 through-point cap directions each. Those finite tests supplement
the above proof-level audit; they do not establish its infinite-union
or all-direction quantifiers.

No substantive repair or additional hypothesis is needed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
